15	package reverseproxy
16	
17	import (
18		"sync"
19		"sync/atomic"
20		"time"
21	)
22	
23	// StreamLogs configures the logging of upgraded streams, such as
24	// WebSockets. When the server has access logging enabled, a log entry
25	// is written to the access logger when a stream is closed.
26	type StreamLogs struct {
27		// If true, the access log entry of the request that upgraded to
28		// a stream (the handshake) is not written. Stream close logs are
29		// not affected. Default: the handshake is logged.
30		SkipHandshake bool `json:"skip_handshake,omitempty"`
31	
32		// The level of the stream close log entries: debug, info, warn
33		// or error. Default: debug.
34		Level string `json:"level,omitempty"`
35	}
36	
37	// Results with which a stream can end.
38	const (
39		streamResultCompleted = "completed" // both directions ended cleanly
40		streamResultError     = "error"     // a copy failed, e.g. a peer went away
41		streamResultTimeout   = "timeout"   // stream_timeout elapsed
42		streamResultClosed    = "closed"    // closed by a config reload or shutdown
43	)
44	
45	// streamAccounting accounts for a single upgraded stream in the stream
46	// metrics. However many paths try to end the stream, it is counted once.
47	type streamAccounting struct {
48		start        time.Time
49		toBackend    atomic.Int64
50		fromBackend  atomic.Int64
51		mu           sync.Mutex
52		result       string
53		finishedOnce sync.Once
54	}
55	
56	// newStreamAccounting starts accounting for a stream that was just established.
57	func newStreamAccounting() *streamAccounting {
58		streamMetrics.active.Inc()
59		return &streamAccounting{start: time.Now()}
60	}
61	
62	// setResult records why the stream is ending. Only the first
63	// result is kept, so the cause of the end wins over its effects.
64	func (s *streamAccounting) setResult(result string) {
65		s.mu.Lock()
66		defer s.mu.Unlock()
67		if s.result == "" {
68			s.result = result
69		}
70	}
71	
72	// finish ends the accounting of the stream, using result unless an earlier
73	// one was recorded with setResult. Only the first call has an effect: it
74	// updates the metrics and reports true along with the final result.
75	func (s *streamAccounting) finish(result string) (string, bool) {
76		var first bool
77		s.finishedOnce.Do(func() {
78			first = true
79			s.setResult(result)
80			s.mu.Lock()
81			result = s.result
82			s.mu.Unlock()
83	
84			streamMetrics.active.Dec()
85			streamMetrics.closed.WithLabelValues(result).Inc()
86			streamMetrics.duration.Observe(time.Since(s.start).Seconds())
87			streamMetrics.bytes.WithLabelValues("to_backend").Add(float64(s.toBackend.Load()))
88			streamMetrics.bytes.WithLabelValues("from_backend").Add(float64(s.fromBackend.Load()))
89		})
90		if !first {
91			return "", false
92		}
93		return result, true
94	}
95	
96	// streamRegistry tracks the upgraded streams that are detached from the
97	// lifecycle of the config that created them (stream_detached), as well as
98	// the upstreams of the handlers that are currently live. A detached stream
99	// stays open until its upstream is no longer live.
100	type streamRegistry struct {
101		mu      sync.Mutex
102		live    map[string]int // upstream -> number of live handlers using it
103		streams map[*detachedStream]struct{}
104	}
105	
106	type detachedStream struct {
107		upstream string
108		dynamic  bool
109		close    func() error
110	}
111	
112	// dynamicLiveKey marks a live handler whose upstreams are only known when
113	// requests are served (dynamic upstreams, or placeholders in a dial address).
114	// Streams started by such handlers stay open while any such handler is live.
115	const dynamicLiveKey = "\x00dynamic"
116	
117	// detachedStreams is shared by all handlers, since the handlers of an old
118	// config are cleaned up while the streams they started are still running.
119	var detachedStreams = newStreamRegistry()
120	
121	func newStreamRegistry() *streamRegistry {
122		return &streamRegistry{
123			live:    make(map[string]int),
124			streams: make(map[*detachedStream]struct{}),
125		}
126	}
127	
128	// addLive marks the upstreams as used by a live handler.
129	func (r *streamRegistry) addLive(upstreams []string) {
130		r.mu.Lock()
131		defer r.mu.Unlock()
132		for _, u := range upstreams {
133			r.live[u]++
134		}
135	}
136	
137	// removeLive marks the upstreams as no longer used by a handler.
138	func (r *streamRegistry) removeLive(upstreams []string) {
139		r.mu.Lock()
140		defer r.mu.Unlock()
141		for _, u := range upstreams {
142			if r.live[u] <= 1 {
143				delete(r.live, u)
144				continue
145			}
146			r.live[u]--
147		}
148	}
149	
150	// add registers a stream to upstream that is closed with closeFn when the
151	// upstream is no longer live. It returns a function that unregisters the
152	// stream, or false if the upstream is not live anymore, in which case the
153	// stream was not registered and must be closed by the caller.
154	func (r *streamRegistry) add(upstream string, closeFn func() error) (remove func(), ok bool) {
155		return r.addStream(upstream, false, closeFn)
156	}
157	
158	// addStream is like add. A dynamic stream, started by a handler whose upstreams
159	// are not known up front, is also kept while a dynamic handler is live.
160	func (r *streamRegistry) addStream(upstream string, dynamic bool, closeFn func() error) (remove func(), ok bool) {
161		r.mu.Lock()
162		defer r.mu.Unlock()
163		if !r.isLive(upstream, dynamic) {
164			return nil, false
165		}
166		ds := &detachedStream{upstream: upstream, dynamic: dynamic, close: closeFn}
167		r.streams[ds] = struct{}{}
168		return func() {
169			r.mu.Lock()
170			delete(r.streams, ds)
171			r.mu.Unlock()
172		}, true
173	}
174	
175	// closeOrphaned closes the streams whose upstream is not live anymore,
176	// and returns the first error encountered. The streams to retained
177	// upstreams are left alone.
178	func (r *streamRegistry) closeOrphaned() error {
179		r.mu.Lock()
180		var orphaned []*detachedStream
181		for ds := range r.streams {
182			if !r.isLive(ds.upstream, ds.dynamic) {
183				orphaned = append(orphaned, ds)
184				delete(r.streams, ds)
185			}
186		}
187		r.mu.Unlock()
188	
189		// closing may block (graceful close writes to the connections), so don't hold the lock
190		var err error
191		for _, ds := range orphaned {
192			if closeErr := ds.close(); closeErr != nil && err == nil {
193				err = closeErr
194			}
195		}
196		return err
197	}
198	
199	// isLive reports whether a stream to upstream may stay open. The lock must be held.
200	func (r *streamRegistry) isLive(upstream string, dynamic bool) bool {
201		return r.live[upstream] > 0 || (dynamic && r.live[dynamicLiveKey] > 0)
202	}
203	
204	// count returns the number of registered streams.
205	func (r *streamRegistry) count() int {
206		r.mu.Lock()
207		defer r.mu.Unlock()
208		return len(r.streams)
209	}

input.summary: I only partly verified this: I read streams.go and a few greps, and the diff was truncated. One blocking problem: the new TestMain in the integration package calls syscall.Exec, which doesn't exist on Windows, so the whole integration package would fail to compile there. CI runs Windows. Coverage looks otherwise solid, and I found no weakened existing tests.

findings.text: TestMain uses syscall.Exec, which is undefined on Windows, so the integration package fails to compile there (CI runs Windows). Because the tests skip when the exec fails, the h2 extended CONNECT criterion (ACC8) is also only met on Linux and macOS. Use a build-tagged helper, or set the GODEBUG setting in code, instead.
TestStreamNotDetachedClosedOnReload only asserts the close within 5s, so it can't show the stream closes immediately when stream_close_delay is 0.
No test covers a stream_timeout expiry or a backend-initiated close producing the right result label in the metrics or close log (integration or unit).
The only skip I found here is the existing GOOS skip in TestHandlerUpgradedStreamHalfClose. I saw no weakened assertions, but I couldn't see the diff for this file.
streamRegistry.count() appears to be used only by tests.

coverage.note: Echoes through the tunnel after two reloads that keep the upstream.
Removing upstream A closes its tunnel while B still echoes.
Checks the stream is open within the delay and closed after it. The delay=0 case is covered only by TestStreamNotDetachedClosedOnReload, which has a loose 5s bound.
Asserts no handshake entry with skip_handshake set. TestStreamLogsDefault asserts the handshake is logged by default.
Asserts the debug level by default. The detached and level-override cases are in the other log tests.
Echoes through intercept with a catch-all handle_response. Encode is covered by TestStreamThroughEncode and access logging by the log tests.
Asserts nothing reaches the underlying writer after a hijack. The 101-is-final check and the encode check are in separate tests.
The test is skipped when the process can't be re-executed with GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1, and the TestMain doesn't build on Windows. A fix that makes it run on all CI platforms would make it covered.
Not read, and the test name is inferred, not checked. Verify that it asserts each stream is counted once when several close paths fire.
Covers valid and invalid input. Defaults omitted from JSON are covered in TestStreamOptionsJSONOmitsDefaults and the caddyfile_adapt file.
Every listed integration scenario has a test. The h2 one has the platform problem described under ACC8.
Recorder and encode hijack safety are tested. Registry and metrics tests are in streams_test.go and metrics_test.go, which I did not read.
